page: Microsoft Azure D96ls_v7 is a compute-focused virtual machine from the Dlsv7 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor with 48 physical cores and 96 vCPUs, operating at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The CPU configuration includes a 480 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache. The system is equipped with 192.0 GB of system memory, yielding a low memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. It does not include local storage or integrated GPUs, but it is Premium Storage capable.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core capabilities and high-throughput execution. The server achieved a top-tier PassMark CPU score of 104,787.21, supported by top-tier performance in extended instructions and encryption tests. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression reached a top-tier speed of 575.95 GB/sec, while single-threaded gzip compression registered at 36.54 GB/sec. Memory bandwidth benchmarks show strong results, with 7,017.2 GB/sec for cached small-block reads and 333.72 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. Redis SET operations reached a top-tier 151.03 million operations per second, and static web serving throughput was recorded at 142.01 GB/sec.

The primary tradeoff of the D96ls_v7 is its low memory density of 2.0 GB per vCPU and the complete absence of local storage, which requires reliance on external network storage. This resource allocation makes the instance highly cost-efficient for compute-heavy workloads that do not demand massive memory footprints, such as web serving, multi-threaded decompression, and CPU-based machine learning inference. For instance, the server demonstrated top-tier prompt processing speeds of 304.72 tokens per second on a medium 7B LLM model. It is suited for compute-bound tasks, batch processing, and high-throughput web serving.
